assets.title: PPFD, DLI & Photoperiod
assets.teachingPurpose: Separate source output, crop-plane photon density, accumulated daily photon dose, and delivery schedule; teach repeatable crop-plane measurement rather than single-point fixture claims.
assets.altText: Educational infographic explaining PPF, PPFD and DLI, showing crop-plane light measurement under a fixture, the DLI equation for constant PPFD, and several mathematically equal daily-light schedules.
assets.caption: PPFD is an instantaneous crop-plane photon-density measurement; DLI integrates photosynthetic photons across the photoperiod. Equal DLI does not by itself establish equal biological response.
scientificNotes: PPFD is expressed as micromoles of photosynthetic photons per square meter per second.
DLI is expressed as moles of photosynthetic photons per square meter per day.
For constant PPFD, DLI = PPFD × photoperiod(hours) × 0.0036.
Interpret PPFD/DLI with spectrum, leaf temperature, environment, crop stage, genetics, canopy geometry and water status.

assets.title: pH vs Alkalinity: Why Buffering Matters
assets.teachingPurpose: Prevent the common error of treating water pH as a proxy for alkalinity and connect source-water buffering to repeated root-zone pH drift.
assets.altText: Educational infographic comparing pH with alkalinity, showing two waters with similar pH but different acid-neutralizing capacity and a flow from source water through fertilizer, media, roots and irrigation history to root-zone pH.
assets.caption: pH describes the current acid-base state; alkalinity describes acid-neutralizing capacity. A water pH measurement by itself does not establish alkalinity.
scientificNotes: Alkalinity commonly reflects bicarbonate, carbonate and hydroxide contributions and is usually reported as calcium-carbonate equivalents.
High alkalinity can increase the amount of acid required to shift water pH and can contribute to growing-medium pH drift over repeated irrigation.
Hardness and alkalinity are different measurements.
Root-zone pH should be trended using a declared and consistent sampling method rather than inferred from reservoir pH.

assets.title: Measurement Quality & Uncertainty
assets.teachingPurpose: Teach that accuracy, precision/repeatability, resolution and uncertainty are distinct; require enough metadata to reproduce and interpret a cultivation measurement.
assets.altText: Educational infographic showing four accuracy-and-precision target patterns, a measurement chain from true condition through sampling and instrument to interpretation, and a checklist of metadata required for reproducible readings.
assets.caption: A reported number is only interpretable when its method, unit, instrument state, sampling context and uncertainty are known.
scientificNotes: Accuracy and precision are distinct concepts and should not be treated as synonyms.
Measurement uncertainty characterizes dispersion attributable to the measurand based on available information.
Display resolution or extra decimal places do not by themselves establish measurement accuracy.
Raw values, units, calibration state, sample identity, time, location and method should be preserved.
